video_title: Is Jaylen Brown A Difference Maker For 76ers? Could LeBron Be Joining? | The Hoop Collective

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: 76ers roster changes after losing Quentin Grimes and Kelly Oubre
quotes.excerpt: I don't think it would have made sense for them to pay him 60 million dollars.
quotes.quote: I want to take a look at the 76ers roster now that it's been so much of a focus on Boston, and rightly so. The 76ers had quite a day on the second day of free agency. They lost Quentin Grimes, who was a nice player for them. I don't think it would have made sense for them to pay him 60 million dollars. They also lost Kelly Oubre, who I thought had a really good year last year. At two years 17 million, which was what the Pacers signed him for, that's good value. He's proven he can defend multiple positions. I like that signing for Indiana.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: 76ers signing Dean Wade to replace Kelly Oubre
quotes.excerpt: He basically replaces Oubre, but he's bigger. He's 6'10, can defend threes, fours, and fives.
quotes.quote: The 76ers also signed Dean Wade. They brought him over from the Cavs on a four-year deal for a little under 40 million. That's Mike Gansey signing a guy that he found in Cleveland and nurtured. He basically replaces Oubre, but he's bigger. He's 6'10, can defend threes, fours, and fives, whereas Oubre is more of a two and three, and I guess four under certain circumstances. They also signed Ariel Hukporti to a little bit more than the minimum away from the Knicks.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Joel Embiid's need to improve as a defender
quotes.excerpt: He's going to have to be a better defender. I saw some metrics that said he was below average.
quotes.quote: Defensively, because he won't have so much offensive responsibility because you have, in theory, Joel Embiid, which always sounds like a good idea and then reality happens, he's going to have to be a better defender. I saw some metrics and some numbers that said he was a below average defender this year. I think that he has the bones of a well above average defender.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: 76ers salary cap situation tied to three players
quotes.excerpt: They have 88% of their cap tied in Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and now Jaylen Brown.
quotes.quote: They have 88% of their cap tied in Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and now Jaylen Brown. Once again, I don't know what we're going to see out of Joel Embiid. When they went home on Mother's Day weekend and it sticks out with me, your arena got taken over and you got beaten by 30 in every game, and that was basically with a running clock. I don't know how Jaylen Brown changes all of that.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown's fit with Jayson Tatum and the Celtics
quotes.excerpt: The problem with the Celtics was Jaylen Brown's fit with Jayson Tatum and his level of happiness.
quotes.quote: Part of the problem with the Celtics was Jaylen Brown's fit with Jayson Tatum and his level of happiness fitting as a co-star and not as the man. This is Tyrese Maxey's team, maybe still Joel Embiid's franchise. So how does Jaylen Brown fit in all that? If Embiid's healthy and he's on the floor, how do those three coexist and enhance each other, not detract from each other?

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Hypothetical scenario for 76ers to recruit LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: If I were Josh Kroenke, the governor of the Denver Nuggets, I would find out what golf course LeBron is on.
quotes.quote: If I were Josh Kroenke, the governor of the Denver Nuggets, I would find out what golf course LeBron is on today and I would fly my plane to that golf course and I would bring along a case of Screaming Eagle. I don't know anything about wine, but I know that the Kroenke family owns this Screaming Eagle winery in California and it's one of the most expensive and rare things you can get in the US. I would have a case of that wine with me and I would have two phones. On one phone, I would have Nikola Jokic face-timing from Serbia saying, 'LeBron, let's play together.' And on the other phone, I would have Rich Paul, LeBron's agent, where I would negotiate a contract extension for Peyton Watson, represented by Klay Thompson, saying, 'Let's make a deal.'
